open_questions: /attributes keys: the target catalogue exposes only the /attributes container, so Color, EU size and Parent style cannot be addressed as explicit nested pointers. They are kept by renaming the source columns to color, size and parent_style and letting attributes_passthrough write them under /attributes. Confirm the resulting keys (color, size, parent_style) are the ones downstream expects.

'EU size' is an integer in the source, so the passthrough attribute /attributes.size will be a number (40, 41), not the string the operator note mentions. Confirm whether a numeric value is acceptable or the attribute must be stringified.

No status, barcode, brand, category or description column exists in this file; those optional fields are omitted rather than filled with invented values (the schema default 'active' for /status applies only if the consumer applies it).

notes: Source has no VAT-exclusive-to-inclusive conversion requirement: 'Tax included' = 'No' in every row, so prices are mapped as given with vat_included=false and vat_rate=0.05 from the explicit '5%' column; no FX conversion or rate inference applied.
Currency 'PHP' and unit 'PAIR' are read directly from constant columns in the file, not inferred from the product type or region.

Parent style, Color and EU size are not top-level schema fields; they are preserved under /attributes (parent_style, color, size) so variant-level data is not lost, per operator requirement that Parent style is not the identity.
Only one price row exists per SKU, so /prices is built as a single-element collection keyed by price_list 'standard'.
Tax rate values in this file are synthetic fixture values, not tax advice.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU', 12 distinct values across 12 rows (unique_ratio 1.0), sku_like hint, already text with no zero padding; variant pattern STYLE-n-COLOR-SIZE confirms per-variant identity.

columns.name: Product name

columns.name: Currency

columns.name: Sales unit

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Header 'Price list'; constant 'standard' is explicit in the file and equals the schema default, so price_list = 'standard' is stated rather than assumed.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Header 'Net price' matches price.amount synonyms ('net price'); numeric, never null, 12 distinct values 1234.56-1356.77, one price per variant — the only monetary column in the sheet.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Header 'Tax included' is an explicit inclusion flag; all 12 rows say 'No', so amounts are VAT-exclusive and vat_included = false must be stated explicitly (not inferred from convention).

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Header 'Tax rate'; all rows '5%', a percent fixture value. Needs parse_number_th percent_to_fraction so 5% becomes 0.05 as a number; the file value is used as-is, no statutory rate assumed.

columns.name: Parent style
columns.reason: Header 'Parent style' with values STYLE-1..3 repeating 4x each — a grouping level, not the identity (the operator states parent style is not the key). No dedicated schema field; stored in the free-form /attributes object under key parent_style. Pointer is the container /attributes because nested attribute keys are not catalogued pointers.

columns.name: Color
columns.reason: Header 'Color', 2 distinct short codes (BLK, WHT) that vary row-wise within a style; operator requires Color retained as attributes.color string. Stored in the /attributes container.

columns.name: EU size
columns.reason: Header 'EU size', integer 40/41 varying within style-color; operator requires EU size retained as attributes.size string. Stored in the /attributes container.
